raw_response:
I am 65 years old and have worked this land for 40 years. I never went to school, so I don't read books or those papers they hand out at the township office. I learned everything by doing it and watching the old folks before me. My husband and I farm 15 mu in Quzhou County. My son works construction in Handan and sends some money home, but the farm is what feeds us. We have a well, so I can water when I need to.

This year I have 13 mu in wheat and 2 mu in garlic that went in last autumn. After the wheat comes off in June, I will plant maize on those same 13 mu.

For the wheat: I used an improved variety that I have grown for three years now. It gave me 1000 jin per mu last year, and the ears are full. Before planting, I put one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — a bag is 100 jin, costs 100 yuan. This spring, when the wheat turns green, I will spread one bag of urea on each mu too. Fertilizer is dear now, but I saw what happened to Old Wang from West Village. He tried to save money and put less last year, and his wheat looked like grass. I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose the crop. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting fertilizer is just a cost. I will water three times: once after New Year if there is no good snow, once when the stems shoot up, and once when the grain is filling. I will spray twice: first for the weeds, then for the rust that came two years ago and made everyone lose yield. I till with the rotary machine after the maize is harvested in autumn.

For the garlic: I keep 2 mu by the well for garlic because at the Quzhou market it sells for good money, better than grain. I plant the big white cloves I saved myself — I never buy garlic seed, that is foolish. Garlic needs a lot of food to make big bulbs. I put two bags of compound fertilizer per mu, one bag of urea, and two cartloads of pig manure from my pen. I water four times: before winter to help it root, when spring wakes it up, when I cut the flower stems so the bulb grows fat, and one more time when the bulbs are swelling. I spray three times: for weeds, for the root flies, and for the white rot that can ruin a whole field. I till it with the rotary machine too.

For the maize: As soon as the wheat is cut in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed. I buy it from the seed dealer — whatever hybrid number they have this year, usually 40 yuan a bag and one bag plants 2 mu. I don't till the ground for maize anymore. The machine plants right into the wheat stubble, no-till, saves time and diesel. I put one bag of compound per mu at planting, then half a bag of urea when the plants are knee-high. Two waters is usually enough in summer because the rains come, but I have the well if it turns dry. Two sprays: one for weeds and one for the bugs that eat the cobs.

I watch my neighbors. If Aunt Zhang puts more fertilizer, I think about it. If everyone is spraying for bugs, I spray too. Change is risky, so I mostly do what I did last year. I expect the wheat to give me 1000 jin per mu, the maize 1200 jin, and the garlic 2000 jin. If prices don't drop, we will be fine.
